draft.title: Aerobic training
card: Aerobic training works the aerobic system, which uses oxygen to produce energy for long periods of effort. Over time it improves endurance, the ability to keep going without tiring.
Continuous
steady effort at a similar pace for a long, unbroken time, such as a 40 minute jog.
Interval
repeated bouts of harder work, each followed by a planned rest or easier period, such as 4 minutes fast then 2 minutes slow.
Fartlek
a Swedish word meaning speed play. The athlete changes pace freely and without a set pattern, such as sprinting to a tree then jogging to a corner.
draft.remember: Aerobic training builds endurance. Continuous holds one pace, interval follows a plan, fartlek changes pace freely.

a.q: Which session is an example of fartlek training?
opts: A run where pace changes at whim, fast then slow
A 45 minute ride at one steady pace
Six 3 minute runs, each with 90 seconds of rest
Five 20 metre sprints with full rest between them
a.why: Fartlek changes pace freely, with no set pattern. The timed runs with set rests describe interval training, which is the tempting wrong choice because it also mixes hard and easy work but follows a plan.
a.clue: Look for the session where pace changes without a fixed pattern.

b.q: Priya is training for a 10 km fun run. Her coach wants her to practise hard efforts of 5 minutes, each followed by exactly 2 minutes of easy jogging. Which type of aerobic training is this?
opts: Interval training
Fartlek training
Continuous training
Resistance training
b.why: The hard efforts and the rests are set in advance, so this is interval training. Fartlek is the tempting wrong answer because it also mixes fast and slow running, but it has no set pattern and the athlete chooses when to change pace.
b.clue: Ask whether the lengths of effort and rest are planned or chosen on the spot.

a.best: A run where pace changes at whim, fast then slow

problems.detail: The clue ('the session where pace changes without a fixed pattern') echoes the right option ('pace changes at whim'), the only option that mentions changing pace. A student can match the words without knowing the idea.

a.q: Which session is an example of fartlek training?
opts: A bush run, sprinting or jogging as the athlete chooses
Six 3 minute fast runs, each with 90 seconds of jogging
A 45 minute ride held at one steady, even pace
Five 20 metre sprints, each with a full rest after it
